races.name: Specialist Group Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Gameball
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with class advantage but 151 days off and faces stamina test over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: C&D maiden hurdle winner; 4th in Grade 2 since; top yard's first-string so a contender
runners_data.spotlight: Impressive winner of a Ballinrobe bumper on debut last year for Andrew Slattery and moved to this yard after; won a C&D maiden hurdle in October before finishing fourth to in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 novice; hood added after a break and seems yard's first-string so a contender.

runners_data.name: Techno Davis
runners_data.note: Unraced under rules but promising point winner making tough debut in competitive novice company
runners_data.comment: Tough race to make his rules debut in for all that connections are respected
runners_data.spotlight: By a top French sire and cost Eur160,000 as a 3yo; won a Kirkistown point on debut in March and is a promising sort but this is a tough race to make his rules debut in for all that connections are respected.

runners_data.name: Alwaysgoinhome
runners_data.note: Complete unknown making racecourse debut with no form guide for this demanding assignment
runners_data.comment: This is a tough race to make a debut in; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam bumper winner, sister to Italian 7f/1m winner Papal Dream (inc 2yo), half-sister to winners Massif Central (Group-placed 1m/10.6f) and Reve Du Jour (6f); this is a tough race to make a debut in; best watched.

runners_data.name: Fort Dino
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 334-day break but has French hurdles experience and strong stable form
runners_data.comment: French hurdle winner; first start for new yard after a break but this is competitive
runners_data.spotlight: By a leading French sire; decisively won over hurdles at Auteuil on second start last May; first start for new yard after a break but this is competitive and stable jockey deserts; tongue-tie on.

runners_data.name: Nadia's Boy
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner but not first string from Mullins yard and faces significant step up in class
runners_data.comment: Beat the useful Frankie John at Listowel; isn't the yard first-string but can be a player
runners_data.spotlight: Unbeaten in a point (2024), Kilbeggan bumper and Listowel maiden hurdle last year, beating the useful Frankie John on last occasion; isn't the yard's first-string but can be a player if ready enough on return.

runners_data.name: Colcannon
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer in good recent form with proven stamina over similar trips

runners_data.name: Immediate Effect
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with juvenile hurdle form who can benefit from expected strong early pace
runners_data.comment: Was poor at Listed level at Naas last time and has to return to best
runners_data.spotlight: Dual AW Flat winner won a C&D juvenile hurdle on debut in this sphere; respectable run in a Grade 1 next time but was poor at Listed level at Naas since; has to return to best.

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse coming off maiden win but represents second string from champion trainer's powerful squad
runners_data.comment: Steps up in class and isn't the yard's first-string but still has to be respected
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden on the Flat in France got off the mark on second hurdles start for this yard at Limerick last time in soft; this is a step-up in class and isn't the yard's first-string but still has to be respected.

runners_data.name: Ionian
runners_data.note: Front-runner from Henderson stable but poor recent form and facing stronger opposition than usual

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 158-day absence with amateur jockey claiming valuable weight allowance
runners_data.comment: Fell in a handicap here when last seen and has to find improvement after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Dual bumper winner including at this track; won at Navan on hurdles debut last autumn but was clinically abnormal when pulled-up at Killarney after; fell in a handicap here next time; has to find improvement after a break.

runners_data.name: Leader d'Allier
runners_data.note: Classy front-runner with Grade 1 experience but suspect stamina over this extended distance

races.paceDynamic: Gameball, Nadia's Boy, Leader d'Allier and Ionian will ensure a strong early gallop over this stamina-sapping trip at Punchestown. The presence of four confirmed front-runners guarantees a searching pace that will test stamina reserves, particularly on yielding ground that demands extra effort. The relentless tempo will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses with proven stamina who can benefit from the strong pace and pick up the pieces late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners engage in a pace battle from the outset
scenarios.body: The searching gallop will stretch stamina limits and set up the race for horses tracking in behind with finishing kicks. Hold-up horses like Immediate Effect and Beauvallon can exploit the pace collapse in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can dictate terms without excessive pressure
scenarios.body: Gameball or Leader d'Allier could string out the field with sustained galloping and prove too strong for late challengers. Their class edge allows them to maintain the tempo while having enough left to resist closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard too early and fold before the home turn
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where tactical speed matters more than stamina. Prominent racers like Colcannon who can avoid the early pace battle will have a crucial positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Novice Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the newcomers Techno Davis or Alwaysgoinhome possess hidden ability
scenarios.body: Lightly-raced horses could exploit the pace scenario with fresh legs and untapped potential. Their lack of exposure becomes an advantage when more exposed rivals hit their limitations.

watchPoints.text: Gameball could be vulnerable to the stamina test if forced into early pace battle after long absence
Watch for market support for Techno Davis or Alwaysgoinhome as unknown quantities with potential upside
Leader d'Allier's stamina limitations may be exposed if the pace becomes too strong over this trip
Immediate Effect needs the front-runners to go fast early to set up his hold-up running style
Fort Dino's fitness after 334 days off will be crucial given the demanding pace scenario expected

races.name: Close Brothers Irish EBF Mares Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Diamond Du Berlais
runners_data.note: Hold-up style could be compromised by small field but Cheltenham third suggests class is there for Mullins
runners_data.comment: Fine run in the Mares' Novice at Cheltenham; is the one to beat if reproducing that form
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to win over hurdles in France but showed useful form; won over 2m5f at Ludlow on debut for this yard and ran a cracker in the Mares' Novice at Cheltenham since over this trip; is the one to beat if reproducing that form.

runners_data.name: Future Prospect
runners_data.note: Front-running style with tendency to race keenly, needs to settle better after Cheltenham pull-up
runners_data.comment: Pulled-up at Cheltenham but better in a Fairyhouse Grade 1 since over 2m4f; this trip suit
runners_data.spotlight: Smart bumper winner but had a tendency to race keenly; got off the mark over hurdles on debut at Naas but was pulled-up in the Mares' novice at Cheltenham; a better effort in a Fairyhouse Mares' Grade 1 since over 2m4f and a repeat back to this trip would see her go well.

runners_data.name: Alliteration
runners_data.note: Free-going leader who found winning form last time, cheekpieces retained from successful Fairyhouse effort
runners_data.comment: Won a Fairyhouse maiden last time; the cheekpieces worn then are retained; has to do more
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner last autumn got off the mark over hurdles in a Fairyhouse maiden last time on fourth start in this sphere; the cheekpieces worn then are retained but she has to do more in this grade.

runners_data.name: Blue Velvet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for in-form Mullins yard but pull-up last time raises questions about current wellbeing
runners_data.comment: Was pulled-up at Fairyhouse last time; isn't the yard's first-string and has to rebound
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner got off the mark over hurdles (2m3f) at this track in January; not a bad run at Cheltenham next time but was pulled-up at Fairyhouse since; isn't the yard's first-string and has to rebound.

runners_data.name: Adrienne
runners_data.note: Promising prominent runner taking well to hurdles, gets significant weight allowance as four-year-old
runners_data.comment: Fine runs in defeat in strong company; has to find more to win but should be in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Flat maiden has taken well to hurdles, winning a Fairyhouse maiden on debut and running some fine races in defeat since; has to find more to win but should be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Catchabird
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent racer in good form with two recent wins, carries penalty but proven at this level

races.paceDynamic: Future Prospect and Alliteration will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set a genuine gallop from the start. This honest pace should stretch the small field and create opportunities for those who can sustain their effort. With Diamond Du Berlais the only confirmed hold-up horse in a race where the others will all be prominent or forward, the tempo should be searching enough to find out the stamina reserves. This race shape strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the leaders and pounce, rather than those needing to make up significant ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders set a solid but sustainable gallop
scenarios.body: Blue Velvet or Adrienne can track the pace and kick clear when the front-runners tire in the final half-mile. The even tempo allows prominent racers to conserve energy for a decisive move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Future Prospect settles better than previous efforts and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: She can dictate terms from the front and has the class edge to repel challengers, especially with Townend's tactical nous. Her recent Cheltenham disappointment masks her true ability on a going day.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly searching and the leaders go too fast early
scenarios.body: Diamond Du Berlais can use her proven stamina to sweep past tired horses in the closing stages. Her Cheltenham effort suggests she has the class to capitalize on a collapse up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners engage in a speed duel that compromises both
scenarios.body: Catchabird's recent winning form and lower weight could see her sneak through as the classier horses neutralize each other. Her proven stamina over this trip becomes crucial in a truly-run race.

watchPoints.text: Future Prospect's settling - if she races keenly like previous efforts, she'll compromise her finish
Blue Velvet's jumping and travel - any signs of the issues that led to her Fairyhouse pull-up
How aggressively Alliteration goes early - her tactics will determine if this becomes a speed duel
Diamond Du Berlais needs the pace to develop strongly to bring her stamina into play in small field
Adrienne's position turning in - needs to be close enough to use her finishing kick from prominent position

races.name: Mongey Communications La Touche Cup Cross Country Chase

runners_data.name: Vital Island
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 139 days off and age 14 creates significant fitness concerns despite past course success
runners_data.comment: Won this race in 2023, a proper stalwart here and at Lingstown, the years are catching up
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of this race in 2023 and won over a shorter trip here last year, two days after a gallant fourth behind Busselton in this race; also a former winner of the Ladies' Cup; a proper stalwart here and over the banks at Lingstown, but the years are catching up.

runners_data.name: Desertmore House
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly matches expected pace shape with proven course form and recent Cheltenham winner credentials
runners_data.comment: Second in this last year, went one better in November, disappointing run at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Close second to Busselton here last year on cross-country debut; looked in fine shape when beating The Goffer and subsequent Cheltenham winner Final Orders over 3m here in November; pulled up over hurdles the following month; dropped away from the 23rd of 31 obstacles at Cheltenham; obvious chance if on song again.

runners_data.name: The Bosses Oscar
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with useful form but 856-day absence creates massive fitness question despite capable jockey booking
runners_data.comment: Poor form in points since second to Desertmore House at Damma House last November
runners_data.spotlight: Useful hurdler for Gordon Elliott in his prime, three wins as well as second in the 2021 Pertemps Final; also runner-up to Busselton over fences at Listowel later that year; has won only once from 16 starts in points; out of sorts since second to Desertmore House at Damma House last November.

runners_data.name: Vanillier
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with Grand National experience but form has been inconsistent in recent cross-country attempts
runners_data.comment: Beat The Goffer here in February, third at Cheltenham, retains the ability to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Second in the 2023 Grand National; third in successive editions of the Glenfarclas at the Cheltenham Festival, last year when around 8l behind stablemate Stumptown, this year 20l behind another stablemate Final Orders; remote sixth behind Desertmore House here in November; much livelier display when beating The Goffer in February, major chance.

runners_data.name: The Goffer
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ideal for this race shape with strong Cheltenham form and Elliott's 8/66 recent record providing confidence
runners_data.comment: Well below best at Cheltenham, solid course form linked to Desertmore House and Vanillier
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth behind Stumptown in the 2025 Glenfarclas Chase; went on to finish third in the Topham and fifth in this race; twice second over the shorter course here this season, behind Desertmore House in November and behind Vanillier in February; may rebound after below-par effort at Cheltenham.

runners_data.name: Lough Derg Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up tactics suit but 14-year-old veteran struggling this season and amateur jockey creates additional concerns
runners_data.comment: Useful hunter chase form at the age of 11 in 2023, struggling this season after a layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Useful hunter chase form at the age of 11 in 2023, third in the Aintree Foxhunter and in the championship event at this meeting; has been struggling this season after a long absence.

runners_data.name: Busselton
runners_data.note: Hold-up style matches race dynamics perfectly and won this race last year but trainer change creates uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Last year's winner, this season's form a cause for concern, change of scene may work
runners_data.spotlight: Beat Desertmore House in this event in last year when trained by Joseph O'Brien, for whom he won five chases in all, including the 2022 Kerry National; well below best when fifth behind Desertmore House here in November, tailed off at Cheltenham in November, had a first spin for Enda Bolger over hurdles and an inadequate trip at Cork; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Outside The Door
runners_data.note: Prominent style could work if pace stays moderate but 158-day break and amateur jockey reduce chances significantly
runners_data.comment: Useful staying handicap chaser, remote seventh behind Desertmore House here in November
runners_data.spotlight: Seven-time winner, including four over fences; ran a fine race over the orthodox fences when second in a 3m7f handicap at last season's festival; made all to win a Wexford handicap last August before pulling up in the Kerry National; remote seventh behind Desertmore House here in November.

runners_data.name: Shannon Royale
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with tactical pace but bleeding history and poor recent form create serious reliability concerns
runners_data.comment: Has reportedly bled, including when a remote seventh behind Vanillier here in February
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 3m beginners' chase for Gordon Elliott last season; lost form and has failed to show anything like his best since joining this team; has reportedly bled, including when a remote seventh behind Vanillier over this course in February.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits extended trip but amateur rider and inconsistent form make victory unlikely despite staying credentials
runners_data.comment: Stays well and is effective in handicaps at a modest level, first attempt at this course
runners_data.spotlight: Stays well, won a 3m2f handicap hurdle at Ballinrobe two seasons ago; won a chase on good ground at Wexford last summer; pulled up in the Ulster National a month ago on first run since a 12l second at the Listowel festival; first attempt at this course.

runners_data.name: Bodhisattva
runners_data.note: Hold-up tactics ideal and recent Edinburgh National third shows stamina but overall form level appears insufficient for this grade
runners_data.comment: Not at his best on the track this season, well beaten in previous attempts at this course
runners_data.spotlight: Third of five finishers in the 3m7f Edinburgh National at Musselburgh in February, not as good as his second in the same race in 2025; weak handicap form lately; well beaten in previous attempts at this course.

runners_data.name: Benny The Duke
runners_data.note: Hold-up style matches but 364-day absence and weak overall form make competitive showing highly unlikely
runners_data.comment: Winning hurdler, 0-10 in points, remote seventh in this race last year, no apparent chance
runners_data.spotlight: Winning hurdler; 0-10 in points, remote seventh in this race last year; no apparent chance.

runners_data.name: Cavalry Master
runners_data.note: Prominent early but warning about fading in finish makes him vulnerable over this extended cross-country trip
runners_data.comment: Veteran six-time winner, a shadow of his former self in points and cross-country races
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran six-time winner; a shadow of his former self in points and cross-country races, though not disgraced at 100-1 in a handicap chase at Galway last September.

runners_data.name: Walking On Glass
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits but 158-day break and poor recent form including rear throughout last start here creates major concerns
runners_data.comment: 66-1 when in rear throughout in the race won by Desertmore House here in November
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose sort; 4-38 over jumps, 4-30 on Flat; 66-1 when in rear throughout in the race won by Desertmore House here in November.

races.paceDynamic: Vanillier will establish an early lead from his prominent position, likely joined by The Bosses Oscar and Shannon Royale in the opening stages. This creates a steady, sustainable gallop rather than fierce early pace pressure, with the large field of hold-up horses including Desertmore House, The Goffer, and Busselton tracking behind. The cross-country format and 4m1f distance means the pace will build gradually through the middle sections before intensifying from the final mile. This measured tempo and extended trip clearly favours hold-up performers who can produce strong finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and builds late as expected
scenarios.body: The patient tactics suit the quality hold-up horses who can unleash finishing bursts over the final cross-country obstacles. Desertmore House, The Goffer, and Busselton all possess the class and tactical speed to strike decisively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Win
scenarios.trigger: If Vanillier or The Bosses Oscar can dictate fractions and kick clear
scenarios.body: The leader gets first run on the field and builds an unassailable advantage through superior cross-country jumping. This scenario rewards horses positioned to track the pace and respond to the initial move.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Staying Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly testing and only genuine stayers prevail
scenarios.body: The extended trip and demanding cross-country obstacles create a war of attrition where stamina trumps class. Horses with proven marathon credentials and recent race fitness come to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Vanillier gets loose on the lead unchallenged
scenarios.body: The former Grand National runner uses his cross-country experience to build an insurmountable lead that the hold-up horses cannot bridge despite their late rally efforts.

watchPoints.text: Vanillier could steal this if allowed to dictate fractions unchallenged given his Grand National experience and front-running style
The Goffer and Desertmore House represent the strongest hold-up threats if the pace sets up as expected
Amateur jockeys on The Bosses Oscar, Lough Derg Spirit, Outside The Door, Dorans Law, and Benny The Duke create tactical uncertainties
Long absences for Vital Island (139d), The Bosses Oscar (856d), Outside The Door (158d), and Walking On Glass (158d) raise fitness concerns
Busselton's trainer change from Joseph O'Brien to E Bolger could impact his chances despite winning this race last year

races.name: Conway Piling Handicap Hurdle (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Hewick

runners_data.name: Seaniecon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse suited by testing conditions, Jonjo O'Neill Jr booking suggests confidence despite 20-day break
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on lively ground in Aintree Grade 1 last time; cheekpieces may help now

runners_data.name: Karl Des Tourelles
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but fourth in this race last year off same mark, needs to find improvement

runners_data.name: Margaret's Legacy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor recent form over 51 days, question marks over current ability
runners_data.comment: All hurdle runs came in France, with two wins in 2020; others make more appeal
runners_data.spotlight: Posted two chase wins in UK in the last two years but hasn't been at his best on last three starts; all hurdle runs came in France, with two wins in 2020; others make more appeal.

runners_data.name: Da Capo Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent type mixing hurdles and chases this season, 48-day break and inconsistent recent form
runners_data.comment: Ran well in this in 2024;  not a bad run in the Martin Pipe last time; needs a bit more
runners_data.spotlight: Three hurdle wins including at this track and ran respectably in this race in 2024; mixing chasing with hurdles after returning from an absence this season; not a bad run in the Martin Pipe last time; needs a bit more.

runners_data.name: The Big Clubman
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over shorter but disappointed stepping up in trip, 62-day absence concerning
runners_data.comment: Grade 3 runner-up was also 2nd in a Newbury novice last time; this trip is a query
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 2m maiden hurdle on rules debut at Wexford last October; was second in a 2m4f Grade 3 at Navan next time but disappointed in a 2m7f Limerick Grade 2 after; runner-up in a Newbury novice last time; cheekpieces added; this trip is a query.

runners_data.name: Blue Mosque
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with solid form at this trip including at Punchestown, up 2lb from last winning mark

runners_data.name: Daydream Nation

races.paceDynamic: Onewaywest is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start without pressure, setting a steady gallop that won't be testing early. With most runners adopting prominent or hold-up tactics, the pace will be moderate through the middle stages before quickening significantly from the back straight home. The lack of early pace pressure means stamina will be at a premium in the final half-mile as the field closes up. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and strong finishers who can produce their best work late when the tempo finally lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Weak Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Onewaywest sets an uncontested lead without early pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop will suit horses who need time to warm up and can deliver their best work in the final stages when others tire. Hold-up specialists like Seaniecon, The Big Clubman and Minella Sixo can time their challenges perfectly when the race finally develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Take Over
scenarios.trigger: If Karl Des Tourelles, Daydream Nation or Hewick press Onewaywest earlier than expected
scenarios.body: This creates a more honest gallop that will stretch the field and favour horses with tactical speed who can travel strongly in behind the leaders. The increased pace will find out the stamina-shy but reward those with proven form at this trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Late Kick
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains slow until the final 4 furlongs before a fierce acceleration
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with the best turn of foot regardless of position will dominate. This scenario particularly suits those with recent good form who can quicken sharply off any pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Onewaywest gets loose on the lead and maintains his advantage throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows him to control the race completely and kick clear before the field can organise a challenge. His jumping right-handed tendency may not matter if he's clear enough approaching the final hurdle.

watchPoints.text: Onewaywest's right-handed jumping tendency could cause serious interference if he drifts across the field approaching hurdles with 26 runners tightly packed
Several horses carry significant layoff concerns including Ballystone (270 days) and Sign From Above (198 days) who may need the run badly
Multiple 5lb claiming jockeys including Michael Kenneally on Da Capo Glory and Shane Fenelon on Ballykinlar could struggle with pace positioning in such a large field
Blue Mosque and Buachaillbocht both have strong Punchestown form over this trip and could outrun their odds if the pace develops to suit hold-up horses
The Willie Mullins-trained Fillyoureye was pulled up when racing too keenly last time but if settling better could be dangerous off this mark

races.paceDynamic: Dont Go Yet and Escapeandevade are confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace, with Coral River and Birdie Or Bust likely to press from prominent positions. This creates an honest gallop over 2m½f that should set up well for closers. The large field of 20 runners means the pace will be solid rather than frantic, but sufficient to stretch the field. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can find late acceleration, as the early pace battle will leave the leaders vulnerable to late challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Dont Go Yet and Escapeandevade duel hard early and weaken significantly
scenarios.body: The contested pace sets up perfectly for the talented hold-up horses who can find their kick late. Sky Lord and Release The Beast have the class to exploit tired leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Escapeandevade gets first run and kicks clear approaching the last
scenarios.body: His proven reliability and tactical speed allow him to hold off late challengers despite the pace. Coral River's prominent style keeps him in touch for the places.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Birdie Or Bust or Western Diego track the pace and time their move perfectly
scenarios.body: They avoid the early pace battle but stay close enough to strike when the leaders tire. Western Diego's class tells despite recent inconsistency.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is steadier than expected with less pressure on the leaders
scenarios.body: This allows more horses to stay in contention longer, favouring those with tactical pace. The race becomes more tactical and less reliant on a strong finishing kick.

watchPoints.text: Dont Go Yet and Escapeandevade setting unsustainable fractions that could collapse the front end completely
Western Diego's jumping under pressure given his inconsistent chase record and 50-day break
Sky Lord's response to first-time tongue-tie as he needs significant improvement
Golden Joy's fitness after 87 days off and confidence following Leopardstown mistake
Release The Beast and Come Walk With Me as the form horses who could benefit most from the pace setup

races.paceDynamic: Salvator Mundi and Pure Steel will contest the early lead in this small field, with both confirmed front runners likely to set a genuine gallop over this trip. Jacob's Ladder will track the pace prominently while Kopek Des Bordes settles in behind, leaving Irish Panther to come from the rear as the sole hold-up horse. The honest pace should set up perfectly for the prominent trackers and those with tactical speed. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close enough to strike but avoid the early pace battle between the two leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Jacob's Ladder or Kopek Des Bordes get the perfect tracking position behind the pace duel
scenarios.body: The dual between Salvator Mundi and Pure Steel will soften them up, allowing the prominent pair to strike with superior class and fitness. Jacob's Ladder's Grade 3 winning form and Kopek Des Bordes' Grade 1 credentials make them ideally suited to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Salvator Mundi gets an uncontested lead with Pure Steel struggling to match the pace
scenarios.body: Without serious pace pressure, Salvator Mundi's class advantage and Harry Cobden's tactical nous will see him dictate throughout and prove too strong. His recent Grade 1 Aintree win suggests he has the quality to dominate this field when things fall right.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle between the front two becomes too fierce and compromises the prominent runners
scenarios.body: Irish Panther will benefit from a strongly-run race that brings his stamina into play, using his proven course form and hold-up style. His recent Naas beginner chase win shows he's effective when getting the right pace setup to close into.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and come back to the field dramatically in the straight
scenarios.body: Pure Steel's hit-and-miss form could see him fold quickly, bringing down Salvator Mundi with him and creating a messy finish. This opens the door for any of the other three to capitalize on the pace carnage, with fitness and tactical positioning becoming crucial.

watchPoints.text: Pure Steel's inconsistent form means he could either contest the pace strongly or fold quickly, dramatically affecting the race shape
Kopek Des Bordes returning after 51 days off following his Punchestown disappointment - watch for market confidence and early movement
Irish Panther needs the two leaders to go hard enough to set up his closing kick from the rear
Jacob's Ladder's jumping under pressure will be key if he's to capitalize on his ideal prominent position
Salvator Mundi's ability to handle Pure Steel's early challenge will determine if he can use his class advantage

races.paceDynamic: Teahupoo will lead with Kawaboomga, Honesty Policy, Meet And Greet, Jetara and Franciscan Rock tracking in the prominent positions, while Bob Olinger and Jimmy Du Seuil settle towards the rear. The pace will be genuine but sustainable given the extended trip and soft ground conditions, with no confirmed tearaway leader to force the issue early. This creates a scenario where the race builds gradually, allowing hold-up horses like Bob Olinger and Jimmy Du Seuil to use their superior finishing kicks in the final furlong. The race shape clearly favours horses with proven finishing pace who can sit off the tempo and strike late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Victory
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays controlled with Teahupoo setting a steady gallop
scenarios.body: Bob Olinger and Jimmy Du Seuil can exploit their class advantage with devastating late runs that the prominent racers cannot match. The soft ground will sap the stamina of those racing keenly up front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent group can control their position without over-racing
scenarios.body: Teahupoo or Honesty Policy can use their tactical speed to build an unassailable lead before the closers get into gear. Their proven stamina at the trip becomes decisive on testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mullins One-Two Punch
scenarios.trigger: If both Kawaboomga and Jimmy Du Seuil produce career-best efforts
scenarios.body: The stable's tactical advantage allows them to control the race tempo while Jimmy Du Seuil delivers a trademark Townend finish from the back. Kawaboomga's fresh legs after a light campaign prove crucial.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Gate-Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If the principals fail to fire and the pace collapses completely
scenarios.body: Meet And Greet or Jetara can exploit their lower weight expectations and catch the favourites napping with superior race fitness. The first-time cheekpieces on Meet And Greet provide the necessary spark.

watchPoints.text: Bob Olinger settling kindly in rear - if he's travelling smoothly turning in, he has the class to win this decisively
Teahupoo's jumping and early enthusiasm - any mistakes or over-racing could drain his stamina reserves on testing ground
Meet And Greet's response to first-time cheekpieces - the headgear change suggests connections expect significant improvement
Jimmy Du Seuil's recovery from his recent fall - any hesitation at hurdles could compromise Townend's usual late charge
The pace through the first mile - if it's genuinely strong, it will set up the hold-up horses perfectly for late strikes

races.name: JP & M Doyle (C & G) INH Flat Race

runners_data.name: Look Me
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with J Townend up, has winning form at this trip and will relish strong early pace from multiple leaders
runners_data.comment: Second to a promising type in Grade 2 bumper at Aintree, smart second-string for stable
runners_data.spotlight: Went close for Stuart Crawford on debut in a valuable sales bumper at the Fairyhouse Easter meeting last year; made a winning start for Willie Mullins at the same venue in February; proved his effectiveness on less testing ground when keeping on for second behind the promising Forthfactor in a 20-runner Grade 2 bumper at Aintree; smart second-string for stable.

runners_data.name: Bois d'Angos
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits this race shape, though 7lb claimer Buckley takes over and 49 days since last run could be concern
runners_data.comment: Still looked raw when winning at Limerick, will need to raise his game in this company
runners_data.spotlight: Under pressure when exiting three out in his only point-to-point start last season; betrayed his inexperience when around 12l third of four behind today's rival Look Me at Fairyhouse in February; still looked raw at Limerick last month and did well in the circumstances to beat the odds-on Border Lad.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with only one run, hold-up style suits but inexperience against this calibre is significant concern
runners_data.comment: Chased home impressive winner Low Kick (Grade 1 runner on Wednesday) at Naas in February
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to five winners, notably smart Flat performer Raise You and Champion Bumper winner A Dream To Share; chased home impressive 10l winner Low Kick (Grade 1 runner on Wednesday) at Naas in February.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning after 222 days off, previous form at this trip suggests stamina not an issue
runners_data.comment: Took a step in the right direction when second at Navan last September, a lot more needed
runners_data.spotlight: Decent pedigree; made debut at Galway last July, stayed on in the closing stages after hanging off the final bend, finished seventh of 19; took a step in the right direction when second at Navan in September, though beaten 11l; a lot more needed.

runners_data.name: Bon Bon Fizz
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will help create strong pace but may pay for early exertions over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Promising Thurles winner has left Paul O'Flynn to join Gordon Elliott for Gigginstown
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten when falling at the last in sole point-to-point start; sent off 100-1 when an eyecatcher in a Thurles maiden hurdle in February, keeping on well and 5l off the leader when falling at the last; made amends with a wide-margin bumper win at the same venue a month later; has left Paul O'Flynn to join Gordon Elliott in the Gigginstown colours.

runners_data.name: Soul Asylum
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter whose early speed will benefit the closers more than himself over 2m4f
runners_data.comment: Hard to know what he achieved in winning a slowly-run four-runner C&D event in February
runners_data.spotlight: Narrowly failed to win on debut for Colin Bowe in a maiden at Dromahane last November, losing out to Red Acres Max who has since won a small-field bumper at Carlisle for Jamie Snowden; fetched £280,000 at the sales (£40,000 more than the winner); difficult to know what he achieved in winning a slowly-run four-runner C&D event in February.

runners_data.name: Adaboy Mushy
runners_data.note: Made all last time at Leopardstown but faces stronger pace pressure here from multiple front-runners
runners_data.comment: Made all to justify favouritism in eight-runner Leopardstown contest, open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Blue Bresil gelding made all to justify favouritism in an eight-runner Leopardstown contest at the beginning of March; left an impression that he could find plenty of improvement; hooded now.

runners_data.name: Cowboy Casanova
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with Derek O'Connor aboard, consistent form suggests place claims if pace collapses ahead
runners_data.comment: Placed in a point and in two bumpers in Britain, stiff task against Irish bumper winners
runners_data.spotlight: Promising third in a point for Colin Bowe last November; made a good start under rules when second of 15 behind an impressive winner at Newcastle in January; had to settle for third at Uttoxeter last month; faces a stiff task against Irish bumper winners.

runners_data.name: Quiryn
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with Patrick Mullins up, Cheltenham form gives him class edge but must handle pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Stylish winner on debut at Naas, promising at Cheltenham despite racing very keenly
runners_data.spotlight: Travelled powerfully to win first time out at Naas in January; proved best of the Mullins squad at Cheltenham, finishing one place in front of The Wager who took his chance in Wednesday's Grade 1; needs to settle better (was very keen for Paul Townend) but seems to have plenty of ability.

runners_data.name: Outofafrika
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who could benefit if positioned perfectly behind the early leaders, 86 days off a slight concern
runners_data.comment: Produced a bright display to beat a Willie Mullins odds-on shot at Fairyhouse in February
runners_data.spotlight: Won his sole point start for Tom Lacey last year; not particularly strong in the market when making a satisfactory debut for this yard at Leopardstown at Christmas, beaten 10l in fifth behind subsequent Cheltenham winner The Mourne Rambler; showed the benefit of the run when much too strong for a Willie Mullins odds-on shot at Fairyhouse in February.

runners_data.name: Our Trigger
runners_data.note: Prominent style with 3lb claimer taking over, Gold Cup winner breeding suggests stamina reserves for this trip
runners_data.comment: Brother to Gaelic Warrior, beat his three rivals at Gowran on debut, in rear at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Gaelic Warrior; not much pace in the four-runner contest in which he landed the odds in testing conditions at Gowran in January; not among the stable's main fancies for the Champion Bumper, disappointingly tame effort nonetheless.

races.paceDynamic: Quiryn, Bon Bon Fizz, Soul Asylum and Adaboy Mushy will all want to lead or sit prominent early, creating a strong gallop from the start. This sustained pace will stretch the field over 2m4f at Punchestown, particularly on yielding ground that will sap stamina reserves. The pace will be honest throughout with multiple leaders ensuring no let-up, before the race develops into a staying test in the final half-mile. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina who can finish strongly off a solid pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four identified pace-setters go off hard and maintain a strong gallop
scenarios.body: The honest pace will set up perfectly for Look Me and Bois d'Angos who have proven finishing kicks and benefit from strong early pace. Both Willie Mullins runners excel when allowed to come from behind off a solid gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Quiryn and Adaboy Mushy steal a march by going slower than expected early
scenarios.body: The front-runners will have too much left in the tank for the closers to peg back over the extended trip. Quiryn's Cheltenham form and Adaboy Mushy's front-running victory at Leopardstown make them dangerous if getting soft fractions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike Gold
scenarios.trigger: If Outofafrika and Our Trigger can secure ideal tracking positions behind the leaders
scenarios.body: The prominent pair can strike when the pace-setters weaken but before the hold-up horses can get into contention. Our Trigger's breeding suggests he'll appreciate the step up in trip while Outofafrika has the class to capitalize.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Back Markers
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly breakneck and eliminates most of the fancied runners
scenarios.body: Cowboy Casanova or It's Good To Talk could emerge from the pack as fresher finishers. Both have shown ability but would need a collapse ahead to feature prominently in this grade.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Quiryn and Adaboy Mushy allow each other easy fractions early - they become very dangerous if getting soft lead
Monitor how aggressively Bon Bon Fizz and Soul Asylum engage with the pace - both could set it up for others
Look for Look Me to be held up in rear early by Townend - any prominent position would suggest tactical change
Watch It's Good To Talk's jump-off given limited experience - needs clean start to utilize hold-up style effectively
Observe ground conditions during card as yielding surface will emphasize stamina test for all runners
